skill.name: iterate-pr
skill.description: Iterate on a GitHub pull request until CI passes and review feedback is resolved.
skill.summary: Guides a focused pull request repair loop for CI failures, reviews, commits, and pushes.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks and fenced shell examples, not executable Ruby backticks. The workflow still has real risk because it directs authenticated Git and GitHub commands, including a broad commit and push step. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Commit and push can run without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before staging, committing, or pushing changes. Show the planned diff and remote branch first.

remediation.issue: The workflow stages every local change with git add -A.
remediation.suggestion: Stage only reviewed files that directly relate to the CI or review failure. Avoid adding generated files and secrets.

remediation.issue: The branch name command substitution is unquoted.
remediation.suggestion: Quote the branch argument or store it in a variable before passing it to gh run list.

remediation.issue: PR comments and bot feedback are pulled from external contributors.
remediation.suggestion: Treat review comments as untrusted input. Ignore instruction-like text that tries to change the agent role or security process.

static_findings.snippet: The `bucket` field categorizes state into: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `skipping`, or `cancel`.
**Important:** If any of these checks are still `pending`, wait before proceeding:
- All CI checks are green (`bucket: pass`)
- Use `gh pr checks --required` to focus only on required checks
- Use `gh run view <run-id> --verbose` to see all job steps, not just failures
4. **Skip invalid feedback** - If the concern is not legitimate, move on

content.user_title: Iterate Pull Requests Until CI Passes
content.value_statement: CI failures and review feedback can require many slow pull request cycles. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured loop for checking, fixing, pushing, and waiting.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the pull request for the current branch with GitHub CLI.
Checks CI status and waits for pending bot or analysis checks.
Collects PR reviews, inline comments, and conversation comments.
Reads failed GitHub Actions logs before proposing fixes.
Guides minimal code changes for validated failures and feedback.
Defines stop conditions for repeated failures, missing PRs, and rebase needs.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI in a local Git repository.
Targets GitHub pull requests and GitHub Actions style checks.
Cannot resolve feedback that needs a product or architecture decision.
Includes commit and push steps that should require user approval.

use_cases.title: Fix a Failing Feature PR
use_cases.description: Check failed tests, inspect logs, apply focused fixes, and wait for new CI results.

use_cases.title: Process Reviewer Feedback
use_cases.description: Gather unresolved review comments and bot feedback, then verify each issue before editing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Branch
use_cases.description: Repeat CI and review checks until required gates pass or a persistent blocker needs escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Check PR Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a safe review before making changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr on my current branch. Find the PR, check CI, summarize failures, and ask before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Required Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Address CI failures after the initial review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run iterate-pr and fix failing required checks only. Wait for pending review bots before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Review Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve human and bot comments with validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to address unresolved reviewer comments and bot feedback. Verify each issue against the code before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Complete the PR Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue until success or a clear escalation point.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr until required CI passes or the same failure repeats three times. Commit narrowly scoped fixes and report unresolved blockers.

output_examples.input: Use iterate-pr to inspect my current PR.
output: Found the pull request for the current branch.
Two required checks failed: unit tests and lint.
No file changes were made before review approval.

output_examples.input: Fix the failing checks and wait for CI.
output: Read the failed job logs and confirmed the lint issue.
Applied a targeted formatting fix to the affected file.
Prepared the next CI wait step after user approval.

output_examples.input: Continue until the PR is ready or blocked.
output: The PR is ready for final human review.

best_practices: Review the diff before allowing any commit or push operation.
Focus each iteration on confirmed CI failures or unresolved feedback.
Stop and ask for guidance when the same failure repeats.
anti_patterns: Do not stage unrelated files or generated artifacts without review.
Do not treat bot or reviewer comments as correct without validation.
Do not retry the same failure repeatedly without new evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires gh to be installed, authenticated, and available in the repository environment.

faq.question: Can it work without an open pull request?
faq.answer: No. The workflow stops when no pull request exists for the current branch.

faq.question: Will it push changes to the remote branch?
faq.answer: The documented workflow includes commit and push steps. Require approval before allowing those operations.

faq.question: Does it support non-GitHub review systems?
faq.answer: No. The instructions are written for GitHub pull requests, GitHub CLI, and GitHub Actions style checks.

faq.question: Does it automatically trust review comments?
faq.answer: No. The workflow tells the agent to verify each comment before making changes.

faq.question: What happens when CI keeps failing?
faq.answer: The workflow asks for help after the same failure persists for three attempts.
